subject: Culture
title: Inti Raymi Sun Festival
description: A micro-lesson that makes Inti Raymi Sun Festival usable.

hook.text: Every June, Cusco reenacts an Incan ceremony to honor the sun god. Thousands gather at the ruins.

buildup.text: Inti Raymi celebrated the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere and asked the sun to return.

discovery.text: The Spanish banned it in 1572 as part of their campaign to destroy Incan religion.

twist.text: In 1944, local artists revived the ceremony from historical accounts. The modern version is a reconstruction.

climax.text: A festival destroyed by colonizers was rebuilt from memory. Culture can survive its own erasure.

punchline.text: They banned the sun festival. The sun came back anyway.

quiz.question: When was the original Inti Raymi banned by Spanish colonizers?
